review.decision_reason: Geotrek-admin is the documented operational back-office application for managing trails, tourism information, and related geographic data. The current repo grants BSD-2-Clause and contains installation and user documentation. The first public-version commit added the license in 2013; a 2014 Parc national des Écrins procurement document corroborates that the park application was developed in 2012/2013 and already BSD-released on a forge. The reported 100+ deployments are suite-level, not attributed solely to this repository.

government_provenance.note: Official Geotrek project history says the National Parks of Écrins and Mercantour jointly developed the trail-management application and selected publication under a free license to enable reuse. The 2014 PNE procurement specification describes the park application as developed in 2012/2013 and BSD-released on a forge: https://geotrek.ecrins-parcnational.fr/ressources/cctp/2014-03-CCTP-appli-mobile-PNE.pdf. The current LICENSE names the parks among copyright holders.

public_source.note: The canonical repository is public and exposes application source, user manual, installation/configuration guides, and current code history without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The repository contains an actual BSD-2-Clause grant (two redistribution conditions and disclaimer), with copyright attributed to Makina Corpus and the named parks. This claim is limited to Geotrek-admin repository code.

primary_evidence.note: The official product page explicitly names Geotrek-admin and describes it as the back-office application for managing trails, places, and tourism information; it also links the source and identifies the BSD license. The 100+ figure is suite-level and is not attributed solely to this repository.

review.product_identity: Geotrek-admin, the Geotrek suite’s back-office application for managing trails, treks, points of interest, interventions, and tourism data
review.agency: Parc national des Écrins and Parc national du Mercantour (public project commissioners; the broader Geotrek community includes additional public land managers)
review.geography: France (French national parks; Geotrek also has an Italian park partner)
review.license: BSD-2-Clause (Geotrek-admin repository code)
review.family_note: Geotrek-admin is the core management back-office, distinct from Geotrek-rando, Geotrek-widget, and Geotrek-mobile. Do not count those suite components or per-organization instances as separate Geotrek-admin products; the 100+ deployment figure is for Geotrek at suite/application level.
review.status_note: The project history dates Geotrek’s beginnings to 2012, but the first located public-version commit that adds the BSD-2-Clause LICENSE is 2013-05-07: https://github.com/GeotrekCE/Geotrek-admin/commit/b96d7aeb82e75c38397422d7b224f9722b2e6b50. The 2014 PNE procurement specification corroborates a 2012/2013 development period and BSD release on a forge. Therefore 2013 is used for first defensible public licensed source, not the earlier project origin. The official current product page identifies this repository’s back-office scope; no suite-wide license claim is made.

review.decision_reason: gFTL is a standalone Fortran containers library created by NASA Goddard software scientist Thomas Clune, with active public development and an Apache-2.0 grant. NASA's product catalog documents the reusable library, NASA's GSFC bio identifies Clune and gFTL, and NASA technical material identifies it as a dependency of the GEOS climate model. The first verified public Apache-licensed source is the 2018-01-15 commit adding the license to the repository; list as Active.

government_provenance.note: NASA GSFC identifies Thomas Clune as a NASA senior computational scientist and names gFTL among his open-source packages; the official NASA software catalog distributes the library as GSC-17742-1.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Fortran container implementation, docs, examples, tests, and current development history.

eligible_license.note: The repository's actual License.txt grants Apache-2.0; Git history first records that license in commit 513c1d3ae2d21d6fa3489e2c3c5dd4d0a5a71946 on 2018-01-15.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's GSC-17742-1 software record explains the Fortran Template Library's container functionality and open-source release; a NASA NTRS GEOS presentation identifies gFTL as a GEOS dependency (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20230017284/downloads/Thompson_M_Containers_noMeatball.pdf).

eligible_license.note: The repository contains an Apache-2.0 grant. JPL announced the public experience in 2017, when the project source was released.

primary_evidence.note: The JPL source release page documents NASA/JPL's collaboration, the public-facing product, its Curiosity mission basis, and the initial 2017 public availability.

review.decision_reason: The assigned repository is the public G’MIC interpreter/library and command-line framework, with upstream download, build, and usage documentation. It is an independently usable operational image-processing tool developed within a French public research unit; the project maintains current releases and extensive documentation. This record does not transfer the core repo’s license to separately hosted G’MIC-Qt or community-filter repositories.

government_provenance.note: GREYC’s October 2021 news explicitly says G’MIC is developed in its IMAGE team; GREYC’s laboratory page identifies the unit’s cotutelles as CNRS, UNICAEN, and ENSICAEN: https://www.greyc.fr/laboratoire/. The linked GreycLab GitHub repository is the official public source for the scoped core product.

public_source.note: The public repository contains C++ source, build materials, tests, license texts, and project history; the official download page links it as the G’MIC-core source repository.

eligible_license.note: The official 2.1.9 source archive (2018-01-19) and its core notices cover files such as src/gmic.cpp, src/gmic.h, src/gmic_cli.cpp, src/gmic_stdlib.h, and src/CImg.h with a per-file choice of CeCILL-C or CeCILL v2.1; CeCILL 2.1 is the OSI-approved option. This is a file-scoped dual grant, not one blanket repository expression. The separately sourced optional libcgmic C API bridge in G’MIC-community has a CeCILL-B notice and is excluded from this product/license scope.

primary_evidence.note: The official download page links the G’MIC-core public repository, stable source tarballs, platform packages, and explicit Debian/Ubuntu and Windows build instructions for the core command-line tool and C++ library. The separately sourced optional libcgmic C API bridge and other G’MIC repositories are outside this record’s scope.

I could not verify current production use, current official distribution, or continued end-user support; establish one before admission.

government_provenance.note: The official Dutch OSS Register identifies this exact Haarlem repository and Gemeente Haarlem as owner. Its README records Súdwest-Fryslân and Haarlem as municipal participants.

public_source.note: Public Java/Maven source, setup documentation, Docker deployment details, publiccode.yml and EUPL-1.2 license are available without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the root EUPL-1.2 text. The first observed grant-bearing code snapshot is the 2020-10-01 license commit https://github.com/haarlem/zds-stuf-to-zgw-api-translator/commit/4a40f8c152da6247c6833dc75db966d4541199f0; code predates this grant, so the license-bearing snapshot—not repository creation—is used for the year.

primary_evidence.note: README says Súdwest-Fryslân went live with Open Zaakbrug in 2021 and says systems were expected to migrate by 2021-Q3; it also describes the bridge as temporary. Current production deployment or an active official distribution/support path is not established. The linked historical report is https://commonground.nl/blog/view/6a946c44-851a-4a2b-bfaf-8368d886aff7/sudwest-fryslan-live-met-openzaak-en-open-zaakbrug.

review.product_identity: Open Zaakbrug (temporary ZDS-to-ZGW migration translator)
review.agency: Gemeente Haarlem; municipal participation by Súdwest-Fryslân documented in the repository
review.license: EUPL-1.2
review.family_note: Migration bridge between legacy StUF/ZDS and ZGW/Open Zaak; do not merge with Open Zaak itself. README states a temporary role and historical municipal deployment.
review.status_note: Hold pending current operational use, a current official release/distribution, or maintained end-user support evidence; a recent repository push alone does not prove service use.

review.decision_reason: The K2 planet-search pipeline is an academic astronomy research tool by Hannu Parviainen and Oxford collaborators, not a NASA product. Their peer-reviewed 2016 paper explicitly links the k2ps code under GPLv3; use of NASA K2 mission data and a NASA inventory link do not establish NASA authorship, funding, commissioning, or stewardship. The current project URL resolves to the authors' OpenTS successor, which also identifies itself as their academic pipeline rather than government software.

government_provenance.note: The paper identifies k2ps as code implementing the authors' own BLS search and candidate reporting methods and states that it is released under GPLv3; it does not identify NASA as sponsor or steward. NASA K2 data use is not software provenance.

public_source.note: The old k2ps repository path resolves to the authors' public OpenTS successor repository, whose README identifies it as the Oxford K2 search pipeline successor and provides installation and usage instructions.

eligible_license.note: The 2016 paper states that the linked k2ps package was released under GPLv3; the current successor setup metadata declares GPLv2. The code is independently licensed but not government-created.

primary_evidence.note: The primary paper identifies the package's academic authorship and code purpose; no NASA source establishes an agency relationship, and NASA mission data use alone does not do so.

review.product_identity: K2PS, academic K2 transit-search and candidate-reporting pipeline; current successor repository is OpenTS
review.geography: United Kingdom/international academic authorship using NASA K2 mission data; no qualifying government relationship verified
review.license: GPL-3.0 (original K2PS per 2016 paper; current OpenTS successor setup declares GPLv2)

source_rows.metadata_screen_reason: Hand-picked Government apps collection entry; the collection includes civic, guidance, example, and government repositories, so provenance is not inferred.

review.decision_reason: The Department of Health/HSE launched the exact COVID Tracker Ireland mobile app and published its source; the public repository contains the React Native iOS/Android source, setup and run instructions, and an initial 2020 commit with the MIT license. Ireland's official service page documents nationwide use and shutdown in August 2023, and an official 2020 release documents code reuse by other public-health authorities and U.S. states. This qualifies as a clearly labeled Archived historical record: a nationally deployed COVID-response application with government-to-government source reuse.

government_provenance.note: The Department of Health states HSE and the Department led development with government and technical partners, and that the source code for Ireland's official app was published; the official service page identifies the app as an Irish Government/HSE service.

public_source.note: The assigned public archive contains iOS and Android React Native source and build/run instructions. Its first commit (44da0f7, 2020-06-27) is titled Initial commit and includes the published app source.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE grants MIT rights. GitHub's LICENSE file history records the MIT LICENSE in the 2020-06-27 initial commit (44da0f7) alongside the source, supporting 2020 as the first public licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The Department of Health documents that public-health authorities in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Northern Ireland, Scotland, Gibraltar, and Jersey launched apps based on the Irish source. The official service page states the Irish app closed completely at the start of August 2023.

review.product_identity: COVID Tracker Ireland — HSE/Department of Health mobile contact-tracing, symptom-tracking, and COVID information app; repository contains its iOS/Android client source
review.agency: Health Service Executive (HSE) and Department of Health, Ireland
review.geography: Ireland; source reused by other national/subnational public-health authorities
review.license: MIT
review.status_note: Archived: contact tracing ended and the app was switched off in August 2023; GitHub archive was set on 2026-03-09. Retain only as an unusually significant historical national public-health app with documented government-to-government source reuse. Do not imply the service remains operational.

review.decision_reason: The public IGN SDK provides documented, versioned 2D/3D JavaScript mapping functionality, but its material SDK code is CeCILL-B-only. Because CeCILL-B is not OSI-approved and third-party dependency licenses do not grant the SDK code, it is ineligible under the review methodology.

government_provenance.note: The exact repository README says this is the Web Géoplateforme SDK made available by IGN. The IGNF organization is the verified account of the National Institute of Geographic and Forest Information; IGN’s official identity card identifies it as a public administrative establishment under ministry authority: https://www.ign.fr/institut/identity-card.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains 2D and 3D JavaScript code, samples, source documentation, and compile/setup guidance without access restrictions.

eligible_license.note: The SDK’s own 2D and 3D notices both grant CeCILL-B: https://github.com/IGNF/geoportal-sdk/blob/develop/LICENCE-2D.md and https://github.com/IGNF/geoportal-sdk/blob/develop/LICENCE-3D.md. OSI’s approved-license list includes CeCILL-2.1 but not CeCILL-B: https://opensource.org/licenses. Third-party components retain their own grants and do not license the SDK code. No eligible alternate grant for the material SDK code was found.

primary_evidence.note: The exact repository publishes the SDK as a reusable product; the release page documents version 3.5.6 (12 June 2025), while the repository README links installation/use guides for both 2D and 3D variants.

review.product_identity: IGN Web Géoplateforme SDK (historically Geoportal SDK), a JavaScript library for integrating Géoplateforme resources into websites in 2D or 3D
review.agency: Institut national de l’information géographique et forestière (IGN)
review.license: CeCILL-B for the SDK code; no OSI-approved alternate grant located
review.family_note: The 2D and 3D SDK variants are maintained in this same product repository and should not be counted as separate products. OpenLayers, iTowns, and other bundled third-party components retain separate license terms.
review.status_note: The 2016-12-07 initial SDK commit added source together with a CeCILL-B notice: https://github.com/IGNF/geoportal-sdk/commit/730598b6f3e05135a9d224cb5cdd18c7ac5bcac8. Current 2D and 3D notices continue to license SDK code under CeCILL-B. OSI’s current approved list includes CeCILL-2.1 but not CeCILL-B, so the SDK fails eligible-license review; third-party library grants do not change that result.

review.decision_reason: ATAF is a reusable Java test-automation framework published by Munich’s IT@M, with public user/developer documentation and tagged releases through v0.3.4. The exact Munich Open Source page describes its purpose and links the repository; the repo’s release and install guidance satisfy the agency-published reusable-product pathway. The first licensed source commit was a README/license skeleton, so the year is set to the first functional framework-source commit in March 2026.

government_provenance.note: The City of Munich’s official open-source page names ATAF, describes the Java 21 framework and its testing use, identifies it as in-house/MIT software, and links the exact it-at-m repository.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the core, REST, and web modules, source code, README, and published developer handbook. The project is accessible without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The actual root LICENSE grants standard MIT rights and names Landeshauptstadt München | it@M; MIT is OSI-approved. Its presence in the initial public commit predates substantive source.

primary_evidence.note: The agency page names the exact product and use (Cucumber-based BDD and TestNG/JUnit suites), links code/docs, and public GitHub releases include v0.3.4 (2026-08-12) with installation/developer guidance. Together this meets the agency-published reusable product with versioned release and user/install guidance pathway.

review.product_identity: Agile Test Automation Framework (ATAF), a Java framework for Cucumber-based BDD and TestNG/JUnit test automation with optional Jira/Xray integration
review.agency: Landeshauptstadt München (City of Munich), IT@M
review.license: MIT
review.family_note: A standalone test-automation framework, not the Munich eAppointment/ZMS application or its application-specific zmsautomation test suite. Its code is independently versioned and usable across projects.
review.status_note: Although LICENSE and a README skeleton appeared in the 2026-01-07 initial commit, the first functional framework source was committed 2026-03-13 at the cited OSS commit. Public release v0.3.4 was published 2026-08-12; official portal and developer handbook provide usage/setup context.

review.decision_reason: The Munich-specific E-Appointment/ZMS source is publicly maintained as a multi-module monorepo under EUPL-1.2 and is linked by the City of Munich’s official product page. Munich documents its citizen appointment/waiting-time system, the cooperative development with Berlin public-sector partners, gradual introduction since 2023, and a live citizen booking view. The repository publishes versioned tags and a developer handbook.

government_provenance.note: The City of Munich’s official ZMS page links this exact repository as Code and says ZMS was developed at it@M in cooperation with IT-Dienstleistungszentrum Berlin and BerlinOnline Stadtportal GmbH & Co. KG. It states introduction began gradually in September 2023.

public_source.note: The assigned repository is the public Munich-specific monorepo and exposes backend, admin, citizen-view, API, queue, and related modules, with a published developer handbook and public release tags. The README explicitly distinguishes the original Berlin project from Munich-specific adaptations.

eligible_license.note: The actual LICENSE is the European Union Public Licence v1.2, with copyright naming BerlinOnline Stadtportal GmbH & Co. KG and Landeshauptstadt München | it@M. EUPL-1.2 is OSI-approved. This claim covers this monorepo source; external dependencies retain their own licenses.

primary_evidence.note: The exact City page describes the appointment calendar, clerk client, administration/statistics modules, live citizen booking view, and gradual introduction since 2023. It links the source repo and official website; repository tags and developer handbook provide versioned distribution and installation/developer guidance.

review.product_identity: Munich E-Appointment / Zeitmanagementsystem (ZMS), the appointment-booking and waiting-time management system represented by Munich-specific code in this monorepo
review.agency: Landeshauptstadt München (IT@M), in cooperation with IT-Dienstleistungszentrum Berlin and BerlinOnline Stadtportal GmbH & Co. KG
review.license: EUPL-1.2
review.family_note: Treat this Munich-specific monorepo as the ZMS/E-Appointment application family; do not split its backend, citizen view, clerk client, admin, or APIs into independent products without separate evidence. It derives from the Berlin E-Appointment project but the reviewed GitHub repo is the City-linked Munich variant. ATAF is a supporting test framework and a distinct reusable tool.
review.status_note: The repository was created in 2023, but the first explicit EUPL-1.2 grant in this repo is the 2024-09-10 LICENSE commit cited for the defensible licensed-source year. The README’s older Berlin deployment history is not used as the Munich fork’s open-source year. The City page describes staged introduction since 2023, and the GitHub repository has public 2.25.00-muc tags plus a developer handbook.

review.decision_reason: This is the Italian government's reusable Open Catalog REST API, a discrete service that powers national open-source software catalogs. The repository documents local Docker deployment, database setup, configuration, and API use; its actual AGPL-3.0 grant covers the API source; and it has a current versioned release. Admit this API component only, distinct from the crawler, parser, and catalog website.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's official software page describes and distributes the exact tool; the 2025 NASA report explicitly uses PyCycle in an integrated MBSA-MBSE demo. The repository has a versioned release history, install directions, and source-aligned examples.

review.decision_reason: Kadaster has released this reusable Angular/TypeScript component suite as public source under EUPL-1.2, with official installation examples and versioned npm components. Kadaster documents that the same GGC components already power more than 30 operational applications, including PDOK Viewer, the WOZ value service and KLIC Viewer. Treat the multi-package suite as one product family.

government_provenance.note: Kadaster's official announcement names GGC as its own software, announces open release and identifies existing Kadaster applications using it; the exact repo publiccode.yml names the Cadastre/Land Registry/Mapping Agency as main copyright owner.

public_source.note: The exact public repository contains Angular/TypeScript source for the GGC packages, tests, install/configuration docs, publiccode.yml and LICENSE.md; it also links the individual npm packages.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the actual root EUPL-1.2 grant and publiccode owner field. This review applies EUPL-1.2 to the repository-authored GGC source; external Angular, OpenLayers, Cesium and other package dependencies retain their own terms and are not represented as covered by this grant. The official public-source release was announced 2026-05-12: https://www.kadaster.nl/-/onze-bouwstenen-voor-kaartviewers-nu-open-source.

primary_evidence.note: The official announcement says the components are used in over 30 applications, naming PDOK Viewer, the WOZ-value service and KLIC Viewer, then released them for reuse. Kadaster's product site has worked examples and technical docs; an exact example documents npm installation of @kadaster/ggc-map and @kadaster/ggc-models: https://www.generiekegeocomponenten.nl/layer-html-config. The component packages have versioned npm distributions, e.g. https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kadaster/ggc-map.

review.product_identity: Generieke Geo Componenten (GGC) reusable map-viewer component suite
review.agency: Kadaster (Netherlands Cadastre, Land Registry and Mapping Agency)
review.license: EUPL-1.2 (repository-authored GGC source; dependencies retain their own terms)
review.family_note: One suite/product identity across the multiple individually versioned @kadaster/ggc-* packages. Do not turn each component package into a separate entry unless later evidence establishes a genuinely independent product identity.
review.status_note: Kadaster says the components were developed and used internally for over ten years but announced their public/open-source release on 12 May 2026; use 2026 for public licensed source rather than the internal project age. Root EUPL applies to project-authored components, not third-party dependencies.

review.decision_reason: K2ephem has a strong government/product case: its first-party README says it was created for NASA's Kepler/K2 Guest Observer Office, NASA's Kepler/K2 Science Center provides command-line documentation and pip installation guidance, and the public repository has an MIT license plus versioned releases. Hold because the first defensible public licensed-source year is unresolved: PyPI shows an initial source release on 2015-12-31 (1.1.0) and a 2016-01-05 DOI-linked source release (1.1.1), but the exact MIT grant for those earliest tagged distributions could not be verified against the license file at those tags. Current source-level MIT text alone cannot settle whether the earliest licensed year is 2015 or 2016.

government_provenance.note: The project README says it was created by Geert Barentsen for the NASA Kepler/K2 Guest Observer Office; NASA's source catalog maps the official Kepler Science Center K2ephem page to this repository. NASA identifies Ames Research Center as located at Moffett Field, California: https://www.nasa.gov/ames-/.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes Python source and documentation without credentials and links to a PyPI source distribution and versioned GitHub releases.

eligible_license.note: The current first-party repository contains a standard MIT license; the historical tag-specific license was not fetched, which is separately recorded as the release-year gap.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's Kepler/K2 Science Center documents exact K2ephem functionality, install (`pip install K2ephem --upgrade`), and user commands; PyPI and GitHub retain versioned source releases, satisfying the agency-published reusable-tool pathway.

review.status_note: Official NASA user guidance and source distribution exist. PyPI dates release 1.1.0 to 2015-12-31 and DOI-cited 1.1.1 to 2016-01-05; need inspect historical license scope to set first public licensed-source year confidently.

review.decision_reason: Abacus is Kiesraad's election-results and seat-allocation application, delivered as a locally installed standalone binary with official user/admin documentation and per-election release guidance. Kiesraad's official 2026 material confirms that 14 municipalities used Abacus for results determination. The source is EUPL-1.2-or-later with explicit OFL font and MPL testing-file exceptions. Its first EUPL license commit is 2024-03-14.

government_provenance.note: The first-party README says the software is designed and built by the Kiesraad itself with municipal and election-administration users; it identifies the Kiesraad as the independent Dutch elections authority.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Rust backend, TypeScript/React frontend, packaging, release branches, and installation, operational, security, and development documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the actual EUPL v1.2 text and README scope: code is licensed EUPL-1.2-or-later except fonts (OFL-1.1), two named test-support files (MPL-2.0), and dependencies under their own licenses. First EUPL license commit: 2024-03-14, https://github.com/kiesraad/abacus/commit/13d13d05de37c148bf34a14a4aaecfed18256473.

primary_evidence.note: Kiesraad's official GR26 material documents Abacus and reports 14 municipalities used it for election results determination; the Kiesraad also publishes installation and user instructions and election-specific releases.

review.decision_reason: xan is a substantially rewritten, actively distributed CSV command-line tool developed by Sciences Po’s médialab for the lab’s daily research/data workflows. It has comprehensive user documentation, multiple installation channels, and versioned binary releases. The source is public and dual-licensed under Unlicense or MIT; agency attribution is to the IEP de Paris public institution through its médialab research unit, with the private FNSP governance nuance recorded.

government_provenance.note: The Ministry’s research-structure register identifies médialab as a Sciences Po research unit and lists the IEP de Paris/FNSP establishment. IEP de Paris is legally a public EPCSCP, although it is managed by the separate private FNSP: https://www.sciencespo.fr/en/legal-terms/. The exact official product page says xan was forked, substantially rewritten, and adapted by the lab for its daily use.

public_source.note: The repository is public and contains the Rust source, tests, extensive user reference, install guides, and release assets.

eligible_license.note: The public repository includes UNLICENSE and LICENSE-MIT; its licensing and Cargo metadata present the product as Unlicense OR MIT, allowing users to select either eligible grant. The current MIT grant is at https://github.com/medialab/xan/blob/master/LICENSE-MIT. Earlier 2015 grant history is imported xsv history and is not used to date xan.

primary_evidence.note: The official product page identifies xan by name, links the exact source repo, describes the CSV-processing command-line tool, and says the lab extensively rewrote it for daily use. The repo’s current README documents installation through Cargo and package managers, command/reference docs, and prebuilt releases.

review.product_identity: xan, a Rust command-line tool for processing, querying, and visualizing large CSV and related tabular datasets
review.agency: Médialab research unit of the Institut d’études politiques de Paris (IEP de Paris, a public EPCSCP; IEP is managed within the dual Sciences Po structure by the private FNSP)
review.license: Unlicense OR MIT (dual-licensed; user may choose either grant)
review.family_note: xan began as a fork of xsv but its official product page says the médialab extensively rewrote and expanded it for its own research/data-collection workflows. Count xan as this distinct product, not as the upstream xsv or the entire médialab software portfolio.
review.status_note: GitHub records this repository’s creation on 2018-07-10. A substantive xan-specific source change to src/config.rs is publicly recorded in the repository on 2018-07-11: https://github.com/medialab/xan/commit/bf799a5090d7cbd313e1d7cd15853f02e68340a0; the repository includes the Unlicense and MIT grants. The 2015 license commit in imported history belongs to upstream BurntSushi/xsv and is not treated as evidence that xan itself was public then. The official product page verifies the current product identity and lab use; current releases establish ongoing distribution. Sciences Po’s legal terms distinguish the public IEP from the private FNSP that manages it.

The exact text and scope of the repository's LICENSE.md were not verifiable, so this row is not admitted.

review.decision_reason: GeoQ is real NGA-developed MIT software with publicly available Django source, install/run instructions, and documented historical disaster-response coordination with NGA/FEMA. However, the default develop branch commit feed ends 2020-09-16 (over 6 years ago), and I found no current product-specific government deployment or support signal; GitHub's newer pushed_at reflects activity outside the default branch. Hold pending current-use/source-parity evidence or an explicit archived-history determination.

government_provenance.note: The White House OSTP report describes GeoQ as developed in coordination with NGA, the Presidential Innovation Fellows program, FEMA, and disaster analysts. The project README says NGA developed the software with MITRE and released it under MIT.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Django application and installation/run instructions. The assigned develop branch commit feed is public; its latest commit is 2020-09-16.

eligible_license.note: The project root contains an MIT grant. GitHub history shows the LICENSE was first created on 2014-06-23 (commit b2b38fb), establishing 2014 as the first public licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The White House report establishes historical disaster-response purpose and government collaboration, but it is from 2014. No current product-specific deployment/support or independent current use was found, and no post-2020 default-branch code activity was found.

review.decision_reason: This is a substantial and active cross-government community Storybook of Mijn Omgeving portal templates, but the repository calls itself Work in Progress and its root npm package is marked private at 1.0.0-alpha.0; no public versioned product distribution or independently documented template deployment was found. Hold until an agency/community release and a concrete adopted/reusable template path are verified.

government_provenance.note: The official NL Design System community page says this exact template initiative is a collaboration including BZK, MijnOverheid/Logius, VNG, Justitie en Veiligheid, and municipalities; the repository’s publiccode names the NL Design System Community as owner.

public_source.note: The Storybook/templates source, packages, docs and live GitHub Pages Storybook are public.

eligible_license.note: The source is explicitly EUPL-1.2 and docs CC0-1.0; NOTICE.md restricts logos/house styles and warns bundled fonts may need separate licenses.

primary_evidence.note: The initiative page describes reusable templates and implementation guidance, but the repo itself says Work in Progress and `package.json` marks the root 1.0.0-alpha.0 package private; no public tagged release or specific deployed consumer of this repository was verified.

review.product_identity: MijnServices Storybook and portal-template collection for government Mijn Omgevingen
review.agency: NL Design System Community (cross-government collaboration including BZK, Logius, VNG and municipalities)
review.license: EUPL-1.2 source; CC0-1.0 documentation; proprietary branding/fonts excluded or separately licensed
review.family_note: The repository is a portal-template Storybook within the wider NL Design System/MijnServices community, not the operational MijnServices portal product. Do not conflate it with separate municipal portals/components.
review.status_note: Official community work began in 2024, but that initiative date is not treated as first licensed product-source year. Need a public versioned package/release or direct consumer/deployment tied to this repository, plus precise agency/community product ownership.

review.decision_reason: IMWO is a conceptual data/information model for the building sector, not an executable application or software component. The repository’s publiccode assigns CC-BY-4.0, which is not an OSI-approved software license or public-domain dedication; the exact source credits Stichting digiGO rather than a verified government publisher. It therefore does not meet this software collection’s scope.

government_provenance.note: The exact source manifest names Stichting digiGO as copyright owner and maintainer. The Open Source Register listing attributes it to VNG, but no primary evidence was found that a government agency owns or commissioned this model; the national building-sector policy context alone does not establish that.

public_source.note: The repository exposes conceptual model/specification artifacts and a functional report, not a runnable program or deployable software source.

eligible_license.note: The declared CC-BY-4.0 license is a content/data license, not an OSI-approved software grant, and no separate OSI license/public-domain dedication for software was located.

primary_evidence.note: Its description identifies a conceptual information model for interoperable building data; this repository is a semantic standard/model artifact rather than an operational software product.

review.product_identity: Conceptual Informatiemodel Woongebouwen (IMWO), a semantic building-information model
review.agency: Stichting digiGO (government publisher/commissioner not verified)
review.license: CC-BY-4.0 for the model/content; no eligible software license established
review.family_note: A conceptual information model intended to support data exchange in the built-environment sector; distinguish model/standard content from software implementations that may consume it.
review.status_note: Reject for this OSS software inventory: model-only repo, no runnable application, no OSI-approved software license; government attribution conflicts between source PublicCode (Stichting digiGO) and third-party collection metadata (VNG).

public_source.note: The canonical nysenate repository is public and contains the API implementation and documentation; its README identifies the project as from the New York State Senate.

eligible_license.note: The Senate licensing notice provides BSD or GPL version 3 for Senate-created code and specifies that pre-existing components retain their stated licensing conditions. The first preserved repository LICENSE commit is dated 2010-08-13 (https://github.com/nysenate/OpenLegislation/commit/d4cb1ce98448b3e8c7cd927ab100650226975b64); although the Senate 2010 announcement retrospectively reports open-source code snapshots in 2009, it does not name their license terms, so 2010 is the first defensible licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The official New York State Senate legislation API is the deployed OpenLegislation service; the Senate announcement links the service and the source project and documents its public release.

review.decision_reason: The ONS Design System is an actively released, npm-installable design system with official ONS service-manual guidance for installation, components, prototyping and use in ONS services. Its public repository grants MIT terms; 2018 is supported by the first license commit.

government_provenance.note: ONS publishes and maintains the design-system guidance in its official service manual; the repo README points consumers to that manual.

public_source.note: The ONSdigital repository is public and includes reusable design-system source and release instructions.

eligible_license.note: The repository LICENSE grants MIT terms; the first LICENSE commit is dated 2018-12-21 (https://github.com/ONSdigital/design-system/commit/3b9fa52cfbca27b64d14e699922b6ad40cd48846).

primary_evidence.note: ONS documents how to install the package and use its components/templates; each release is published as @ons/design-system.

review.agency: Office for National Statistics (ONS), Design System team
review.license: MIT
review.family_note: ONS-specific design system, distinct from GOV.UK Design System.

government_provenance.note: The official data.gouv.fr engineering article says Etalab, the government agency responsible for data.gouv.fr, developed and operated the platform and maintained most udata commits. Current project publiccode additionally names DINUM as a funder.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Python application and services, README, documentation links, and release history.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE is the full GNU AGPL v3 text and publiccode.yml declares AGPL-3.0-only, but current pyproject.toml says license = { text = "MIT" }. No authoritative scope statement reconciles these conflicting project-wide declarations; do not infer that one is stale.

primary_evidence.note: The official article identifies udata as the core API/business-logic and source of truth behind the data.gouv.fr catalog, and reports reuse by the governments of Serbia and Luxembourg. The project has user/developer docs and versioned releases.

review.decision_reason: Government sponsorship, public source, MIT licensing, and a 2021 source/license year are supported. However, the exact official evidence describes Jitsi Box as a prototype and “message in a bottle” inviting teachers to test it, with a more complete product conditional on demand. The 2022 classroom experiment is real but appears to be pilot-stage rather than independent reuse, a production operational tool, or a versioned agency-published product; hold pending evidence of subsequent deployment/reuse or a maintained versioned distribution.

government_provenance.note: The official FUN announcement states that France Université Numérique and CentraleSupélec’s Digital Lab developed this exact Jitsi Box prototype. FUN’s official About page identifies France Université Numérique as a GIP: https://www.fun-mooc.fr/fr/a-propos/.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the React application, Raspberry Pi controller materials, setup guidance, and no-access-barrier source code.

eligible_license.note: The repository contains an actual MIT license and the README states the work is released under the MIT License. Git history shows the license was added on 2021-11-29 (https://github.com/openfun/jitsi-box/commit/bd539bdf4424e350abece77ef47d53368b59d59e).

primary_evidence.note: The exact official announcement calls this a first operational prototype and explicitly frames it as a call for teacher adoption before a more advanced version could be made. A later official account reports classroom experiments in several Vosges collèges (https://www.fun-mooc.fr/fr/actualites/retour-sur-les-experimentations-de-la-jitsi-box-en-classe/), but I found no evidence that the source became a maintained production tool, independently reused deployment, or versioned product release. Pilot activity plus a DIY setup guide alone does not clear the notability baseline.

review.product_identity: Jitsi Box, a Raspberry Pi/touchscreen classroom hybrid-conferencing prototype built around Jitsi
review.agency: France Université Numérique (GIP) and CentraleSupélec Digital Lab
review.license: MIT
review.family_note: Jitsi Box is a bespoke hybrid-classroom device/app integrating the separate Jitsi meeting system; do not count upstream Jitsi or the hosted demo as part of this repository’s product/license scope.
review.status_note: Functional source appears in the repository from November 2021 and the MIT grant was added on 2021-11-29. Official evidence documents a pilot and conference demonstrations in 2022, but not post-pilot adoption or current maintenance. Clear this hold with exact evidence of a versioned release plus installation/user guidance, sustained operational use, or independent reuse.

review.decision_reason: GetHelpLex is a Lexington-local Finda adaptation with public JavaScript source and an MIT license, and independent primary sources document creation with support from Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government's SAVI program. The repository README explicitly describes it as customized Finda code, and its latest branch commit was 2021-08-11; the service evidence I found is historical (2015/2016), so current government support/use and whether this local fork merits a separate product entry remain unresolved.

government_provenance.note: The University of Kentucky's 2016 launch report says GetHelpLex was created with support from Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council's SAVI program, OpenLexington, and other partners. A 2016 LFUCG Council agenda also authorized SAVI Program advertising for GetHelpLex.

public_source.note: The assigned public repository contains the local JavaScript/HTML app, Lexington treatment-resource data, test commands, and development instructions.

eligible_license.note: The repository's root license file is identified by GitHub as MIT. Its history predates the local fork, so this review treats MIT as the inherited Finda source grant and does not infer a standalone public-release year for the Lexington customization.

primary_evidence.note: The 2016 source establishes the launch, local treatment-locator use, and SAVI support, but is not a current 2026 service/support signal. Repository gh-pages last changed 2021-08-11; the website/source page did not establish current government use or maintenance. README identifies this repo as a customization of Code for Boston's Finda, so independent product boundary also needs coordinator judgment.

review.product_identity: GetHelpLex — Lexington-specific adaptation of Code for Boston's Finda treatment-locator web app, with local treatment-resource data and customized survey/faceting
review.agency: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government (SAVI Program) in a cross-sector coalition
review.license: MIT (inherited Finda repository grant; local modification's first public licensed-source date not established)
review.status_note: Hold for current-use/source-parity and product-family determination. The 2016 source says the resource launched in October 2015 with SAVI support; the exact assigned repo states it is a local customization of Code for Boston's Finda rather than an independent software family. Latest branch commit is 2021-08-11 (over 5 years old); current government use was not established.

review.decision_reason: This is an OpenUK-led public-code directory data repository, not government-created, commissioned, funded, or stewarded software. OpenUK identifies itself as an open-technology industry body/nonprofit and the 2018 directory launch notice names a consortium of civil-society organizations, not a public administration. The repository's JSON records and database files support a metadata directory; the associated web interface is a separate archived repository. It fails the government-provenance and independent-software identity gates.

government_provenance.note: The repository is under OpenUK, which describes itself as a UK open-technology industry body; the launch announcement names OpenUK, FSFE, OpusVL, and Public Money/Public Code. No government creation, procurement, funding, or stewardship of this specific repository was established.

public_source.note: The public repository contains JSON directory records, database inputs, and entry files.

eligible_license.note: A GPL-3.0 text is present, but this repository is a directory of contributed project metadata; the available record does not establish that the blanket code license covers all embedded third-party metadata. This is not outcome-determinative because government provenance fails.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party project launch describes a curated/federated directory that gathers information about public-administration-funded software; this repository stores directory data. The separate OpenUK web-interface repository is distinct, so this URL does not identify a government software product.

review.product_identity: OpenUK Public Code Directory metadata collection/data repository, not government software; distinct from the separate archived web-interface repository
review.agency: No government agency relationship established; OpenUK is a civil-society/industry organization
review.license: GPL-3.0 license text is present; scope over embedded third-party metadata unresolved
review.status_note: Repo last pushed 2021-10-22; the companion web-interface repo is listed as archived in OpenUK's organization profile. Rejected for government provenance and product identity; do not equate directory records with individually reviewed catalog software.

review.decision_reason: OWC Accessible Docs is a real installable WordPress plugin with usable source and instructions, but its exact municipal publisher/deployment and release path are unresolved. The source is under the OpenWebconcept community while PublicCode and code name Yard as owner/author; I found official evidence that OWC is a 30+ municipality collaboration co-founded by Yard, but no primary page ties this exact plugin to a named municipality or live deployment. The plugin also depends on an external NLDoc processing service.

government_provenance.note: The official OWC partner page describes a shared municipal software collaboration with 30+ participating municipalities and identifies Yard as co-founder/implementation partner; this exact repository names the plugin OWC Accessible Docs and Yard as author, but no municipal commissioner or official adopter for this plugin was found.

public_source.note: The public WordPress plugin implementation, setup files and bundled source are accessible; README provides manual/WordPress installation and usage steps.

eligible_license.note: The root has a full EUPL-1.2 grant; README and the main plugin PHP header also declare GPL-2.0-or-later. Both are OSI-approved, but the exact dual-license scope needs owner clarification; bundled vendor-prefixed dependencies retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: README gives real plugin installation and use, and the main plugin file has version 0.0.1, but there is no tag/release, public official service page or municipal deployment tied to this plugin. It sends files to the external NLDoc service, which is not part of this repository.

review.product_identity: OWC Accessible Docs WordPress plugin (requires external NLDoc document-processing service)
review.agency: OpenWebconcept municipal collaboration; Yard Digital Agency (co-founder/implementation partner; exact commissioning municipality unverified)
review.license: EUPL-1.2 root grant; main plugin/README also say GPL-2.0-or-later (both eligible; scope expression unresolved)
review.family_note: Plugin code is source-available and installable, but the NLDoc document conversion/status platform is an external service and is not included or licensed by this repository. Do not imply the plugin alone provides document conversion.
review.status_note: Initial public commit is dated 2025-02-18 and contains plugin code plus EUPL text; main file declares 0.0.1 and GPL-2.0-or-later. Hold until an official municipal/OWC page identifies this exact plugin in use and owner confirms grants/dependency boundary.

review.decision_reason: GeoNature is an operational biodiversity information system with current installation, administrator, and user documentation and a public-sector deployment community. The exact repository is a maintained product, not the broader PnX-SI inventory. Current code has an OSI-approved GPL-3.0 grant; the repository retains an older 2014 BSD-3-Clause notice as well, so both in-scope root notices are recorded rather than silently collapsed.

government_provenance.note: The GeoNature project presentation identifies Parc national des Écrins as developer and owner of the original GeoNature rights and documents deployments by other parks and biodiversity bodies. The official project site describes the maintained collective as national parks and other biodiversity actors.

public_source.note: The assigned canonical GitHub repository is public and contains the current backend/frontend application, tests, install/migration scripts, and docs.

eligible_license.note: The current root LICENSE is the full GPL-3.0 text. The repository also retains `LICENCE.txt`, whose direct grant is BSD-3-Clause and whose first committed version is at https://github.com/PnX-SI/GeoNature/commit/6cbc44652e4c7058b5c91eea87d0f826f3e1c98d. Both named grants are OSI-approved; this row does not extend them to bundled biodiversity records or external modules.

primary_evidence.note: Current official documentation gives global and standalone installation steps, configuration, service startup, and links to user/admin manuals. The current documentation identifies release 2.17.5; separate GeoNature products such as TaxHub, UsersHub, Atlas, and mobile clients are not included in this repository identity.

review.product_identity: GeoNature, the web biodiversity-observation and biodiversity-data management application in the PnX-SI ecosystem
review.agency: Parc national des Écrins (originating developer/rights holder), within the PnX-SI national-parks and biodiversity-agency collaboration
review.license: GPL-3.0 (current root LICENSE); historical BSD-3-Clause LICENCE.txt also retained
review.family_note: Review only the GeoNature core repository. The project site describes separately installable sibling tools (TaxHub, UsersHub, GeoNature-atlas, GeoNature-citizen, and mobile tools); do not treat those as covered by this repository license or merge them into one software identity.
review.status_note: The 2014-12-01 `LICENCE.txt` commit contains the Parc national des Écrins BSD-3-Clause grant and is the earliest directly identified public licensed-source snapshot. A later root LICENSE is standard GPL-3.0. Both are OSI-approved; publication should display both existing notices or have the coordinator resolve whether the later root grant supersedes the historical notice. The current product is separately documented at version 2.17.5.

review.decision_reason: The Province of Zuid-Holland's Omgevingsbeleid front end is the deployed public policy viewer and authorized policy-editor UI for the province's digital environmental-policy platform. Its actual EUPL-1.2 source is public and the provincial platform describes this front-end and its neighboring API/publication components. The identity is limited to this repository's front-end, not the full backend/publishing stack.

government_provenance.note: The manifest identifies the Province of Zuid-Holland as contractor and gives its official project contact; the Province's platform page links to the separate front-end and API repositories.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the React/TypeScript web front end, build/test instructions, API client code, and deployment configuration without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the actual LICENSE.md text: EUPL v1.2. This finding applies to the front-end repository only; dependencies and separate service repositories retain their own licenses.

primary_evidence.note: The Province's live platform explains the public policy viewer, authenticated editing environment, and publication connection to the national official-publications facility; the provincial repository is the front-end code for that deployed service.

review.product_identity: Omgevingsbeleid Frontend: Province of Zuid-Holland public viewer and authorized policy-editor UI
review.agency: Province of Zuid-Holland (Provincie Zuid-Holland)
review.license: EUPL-1.2 for this front-end repository; dependencies and separate platform services retain their own licenses
review.family_note: This row is the front-end only. The API and DSO/publishing components are separate repositories/services; do not claim their code or licenses from this UI repository or merge those component repositories into this entry without separate review.
review.status_note: Although publiccode.yml lists a 2019-03-25 releaseDate, the first LICENSE.md was added at https://github.com/Provincie-Zuid-Holland/Omgevingsbeleid-Frontend/commit/6c2a6dd5cc28f42d4d67ab03a1eede98b0af9197 dated 2021-01-15; use 2021 as the first defensible licensed-source year.

review.decision_reason: This is an official open-source release of CHVote v1's offline election-administration application plus the utility libraries it needs, not the complete online voting platform. The repository identifies the Geneva State Chancellery and Geneva IT Department as collaborators, publishes AGPL-3.0 code and detailed build/run guidance, and Geneva's 2017 announcement identifies this exact released component and records use of the larger CHVote platform by six cantons. The operational platform was discontinued in 2019 and this repository was archived in 2026; retain only as an historically significant, multi-canton election-software component, with the scope limitation explicit.

government_provenance.note: The repository README says CHVote resulted from collaboration between the Geneva State Chancellery and Geneva IT Department; Geneva's official 2017 release page confirms the canton published the source.

public_source.note: The public repository provides the offline administration application's source, utility libraries, documentation, and build/run steps.

eligible_license.note: The repository license and README release the components under GNU AGPL version 3.0, an OSI-approved license; this claim is scoped to the published offline application and included utilities, not undisclosed platform components.

primary_evidence.note: Geneva's official announcement says the previously published source was the component used to generate encryption keys and decrypt the ballot box, records substantial public review, and a separate Geneva release reports CHVote was used by six cantons. The repository supplies compiling/running guidance. Geneva later discontinued v1 operation in 2019; the historical importance is the publicly audited election component and multi-canton service, not current use.

review.product_identity: CHVote v1 offline administration application and required utility libraries; one security-critical released component, not the complete CHVote online voting system
review.agency: State Chancellery and General Directorate of Information Systems, Republic and Canton of Geneva
review.geography: Geneva, Switzerland; CHVote service used in six Swiss cantons in 2017
review.license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)
review.status_note: Archived / historical. The source repo was archived on 2026-05-22. Geneva ended CHVote v1 operations in 2019. The only admitted identity is the released offline administration app plus required utilities; do not describe this repository as the full voting platform.

review.decision_reason: Magrit is a live, versioned thematic-cartography web/desktop application with a detailed user manual, examples, and training resources. RIATE is a CNRS/Université Paris Cité research unit; the current official application states GPL-3.0-or-later and links this exact source. Its established teaching and research-tool pathway is product-specific.

government_provenance.note: The official RIATE site identifies UAR 2414 as a joint research support unit of CNRS and Université Paris Cité and directly links Magrit. The official Magrit site credits CNRS UAR 2414 RIATE.

public_source.note: The current canonical repository is public and exposes browser and desktop application source, build scripts, examples, documentation, and release notes.

eligible_license.note: The repository root carries a full GNU GPL v3 license; current first-party Magrit documentation states GPL-3.0-or-later. GPL is OSI-approved. This claim covers the repository-authored source, not external GIS libraries or map data.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party documentation provides user tutorials, examples, installation/access instructions, feature guides, and release history; the application is currently served by CNRS at magrit.cnrs.fr (version 2.4.2).

review.product_identity: Magrit, an online and desktop thematic-cartography application
review.agency: CNRS / Université Paris Cité, UAR 2414 RIATE
review.license: GPL-3.0-or-later
review.family_note: This row is the named Magrit application only. Do not merge other RIATE mapping libraries, teaching materials, spatial datasets, or repositories from the same research group into this license/product boundary.
review.status_note: The earliest directly inspected repository snapshot is in 2016 and contains the GPL grant; GitHub repo creation and the initial GPL-bearing history are both in 2016, so no earlier imported commit date is used. RIATE and the current official site identify the exact app and live version 2.4.2. The 2018 ICA-Proc article is specifically about Magrit as a thematic mapping tool; the product also remains operational with a full current manual.

review.decision_reason: Pacini-typing is a stable RIVM bioinformatics CLI application for bacterial gene/SNP detection, with versioned releases, Bioconda installation, extensive configuration and end-user documentation. review.decision_reason: The Scottish Government's verified GitHub organization says its Digital Publishing team develops www.gov.scot, and the assigned government-controlled repository describes itself as the site and publishing environment for gov.scot (Hippo CMS-based). Its current public Java source contains a full Crown Copyright MIT grant, it has local-build/run documentation, and the official gov.scot site is the live government publication service. This is a first-party operational government service source, not a repository admitted from the UK organization mapping alone.

government_provenance.note: The Scottish Government GitHub organization is verified against www.gov.scot and states that its Digital Publishing team develops www.gov.scot and mygov.scot. The exact assigned repository is in that organization and is described there as the gov.scot site/publishing environment, establishing a specific team-to-project relationship.

public_source.note: GitHub exposes the current public Java source tree and README without credentials. The README contains instructions to build and run the CMS/site locally; the repository remains maintained in the Scottish Government organization.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE contains the full MIT grant and Crown Copyright 2017-2018 notice. File history records an explicit 'Add license file' commit eaf3784613e54683974197f0bcd113f723bd23ee on 2018-03-29, which establishes the first defensible public grant year as 2018.

primary_evidence.note: The live Scottish Government website is the official, actively maintained public publication service; the verified GitHub organization and exact repository description tie its site/publishing environment source to the Digital Publishing team. The repository README supplies concrete CMS/site build and local-run guidance, supporting the operational-software pathway.

review.status_note: The assigned repo description contains the qualifier 'beta'; the reviewed evidence proves its identity as the Scottish Government's gov.scot site/publishing environment, but not that every current production component is contained in this one repository. review.decision_reason: The Federal Office of Energy documents and operates the public 'Kann ich bohren?' application, an interactive service for checking geothermal probe borehole permission at Swiss locations. primary_evidence.note: BFE describes the interactive 'Kann ich bohren?' application and links the live service, explaining that it uses cantonal data to assess whether a geothermal borehole is allowed at a location. The repository also has versioned 0.2.4 release and deployment documentation.

review.decision_reason: Docs par Archifiltre is a publicly distributed Electron desktop application for visualizing and improving file trees, maintained in the SocialGouv/Fabrique des ministères sociaux context. The official download site provides a current version, installation steps for three operating systems, and reports 300+ users. Current Apache-2.0 scope and 2018 licensed source history are verified.

government_provenance.note: Project publiccode identifies Mission Fabrique numérique (FabNum) as funder and links to its official government-directory entry; package metadata names Fabrique des ministères sociaux as author. The first-party product site is hosted on fabrique.social.gouv.fr.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Electron application, development/setup instructions, import utility, and license.

review.decision_reason: GEPnet is a named Polícia Federal project-office management system, not merely an SPB-account lead. The current Gov.br catalog links this exact repository and identifies the PF as developer; the repository’s top-level deployment note grants GPL 2.0 or later for the GEPnet files, and its user manual/changelog documents version 3.4.3. An official PF 2025 planning document describes GEPnet 2 as an operational corporate solution integrated with PF databases and SISEG. This supports current product use and source lineage despite quiet recent code activity; label Maintained, not Active.

government_provenance.note: The current government catalog’s Gepnet card says it was developed by the Polícia Federal and links directly to this repository. The PF’s 2025 planning document also identifies GEPnet 2 as a solution used to manage its project offices.

eligible_license.note: The top-level GEPnet deployment note carries a 2010–2022 Polícia Federal copyright and grants redistribution/modification under GNU GPL 2.0 or later. The official SPB user manual independently states the version offered through the portal is GPL 2 or superior (https://softwarepublico.gov.br/social/gepnet/manuais-de-usuario/manual-do-usuario-nivel-basico-versao-html-em-construcao?version=6). Third-party dependencies retain their own notices.

primary_evidence.note: The PF’s 2025 project-management methodology describes GEPnet 2 as a corporate project-office management solution integrated with PF databases/SISEG. The repository itself provides user guidance and a documented version 3.4.3 changelog; the official catalog links that source URL to the product.

review.decision_reason: shinygouv is a versioned R package that implements the French State Design System in Shiny applications. Project metadata and government-affiliated maintainer details identify French ministry/territorial government funding and use; the repo supplies installation instructions and user documentation, and an official demo is live. The package’s EUPL scope is confirmed, with vendored DSFR assets noted separately.

government_provenance.note: The project manifest specifically names SGAR Pays de la Loire, the ecological-transition ministry/CGDD, and DREAL Pays de la Loire as funders and names the ministry and DREAL as users, linking each to official government directories. DESCRIPTION also identifies an author with a developpement-durable.gouv.fr email.

public_source.note: The public Git repository includes R package source, README installation and examples, vignettes, docs, tests, publiccode metadata, and a version tag.

eligible_license.note: The top-level LICENSE is the EUPL v1.2 text; DESCRIPTION and project documentation explicitly state EUPL (>= 1.2), supporting EUPL-1.2-or-later for package code. Vendored DSFR v1.9.3 assets have a separate MIT notice excluding the Marianne font; the product license note does not claim every included asset is EUPL.

primary_evidence.note: The documentation provides package guidance, links a live Shiny demo, and describes implementation of the French State Design System. README gives an install command; the repository has version tag v1.0.4 and publiccode metadata gives its release date as 2024-07-26.

review.product_identity: shinygouv, R package implementing DSFR components and tools for Shiny applications
review.agency: SGAR Pays de la Loire; Ministry for Ecological Transition / CGDD; DREAL Pays de la Loire (project-named funders; ministry and DREAL also listed as users)
review.license: EUPL-1.2-or-later
review.family_note: This is a reusable Shiny implementation of the DSFR, distinct from the underlying State Design System and from individual Shiny applications built with the package. Vendored DSFR v1.9.3 assets have a separate MIT notice; Marianne font is excluded.
review.status_note: Initial package/license commit is 2022-07-11. The project has versioned tag v1.0.4 (2024-07-26 in its publiccode metadata), official docs and a live demo. Package code is EUPL >=1.2; vendored DSFR asset terms remain separately scoped.

review.decision_reason: The Canton of Zurich Office for Statistics and Data publishes a versioned, installable Web Components library implementing the cantonal design system. The package is independently reusable across frontend stacks and has a public Storybook user guide; its beta warning is retained, not treated as production adoption.

government_provenance.note: The exact publiccode manifest identifies Canton Zurich, its Office for Statistics and Data contact, government scope, and use by the canton.

public_source.note: The library implementation, build/test setup, package files, and component examples are public.

eligible_license.note: The initial 2023 source snapshot contains an MIT grant and the package implementation; the current source license is also MIT. Fonts are deliberately excluded and must be separately licensed by consumers.

primary_evidence.note: README documents npm installation, browser/CDN use, component examples, and links to a detailed Storybook guide; current package usage is versioned (0.22.0). The README explicitly warns this is active/beta development without a major release.

review.product_identity: Leu, the Canton of Zurich’s framework-agnostic Web Components implementation of its design system
review.agency: Amt für Statistik und Daten (Office for Statistics and Data), Canton of Zurich
review.license: MIT (code); fonts are excluded/not bundled
review.family_note: This is the canton’s reusable Web Components implementation (npm package @statistikzh/leu), distinct from the underlying visual design rules and distinct from federal design-system products. Do not imply the package includes licensed fonts.
review.status_note: Initial commit 5726c2fd2c7738093d4deec2ccce27daa3cd733d (2023-08-30) contains the MIT license and package source. Current publiccode releaseDate is 2023-11-15; package/readme show current 0.22.0 usage. Development status is beta: no major release has shipped, minor versions may break, and maintainers request contact before production use. This still meets the agency-published reusable-product path via versioned package and installation/user docs; do not overstate production deployment.

review.decision_reason: Open Zaakbrug is a municipality-led, versioned Java bridge that lets legacy ZDS case-management applications communicate with the newer ZGW/OpenZaak APIs. The municipal repository supplies an EUPL-1.2 grant, installation documentation, Docker distribution, and a current versioned release; its README identifies municipal production deployments. This is an operational migration tool, not the OpenZaak case system itself.

government_provenance.note: The verified Gemeente Súdwest-Fryslân organization publishes this exact repo. Its README says the bridge began in 2019 with Súdwest-Fryslân, Utrecht, and Haarlem and VNG innovation funding; it lists the municipality and other municipal production uses.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Java application, configuration, tests, documentation, Docker build/distribution links, and source history without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Inspected the root EUPL v1.2 license text; GitHub also detects EUPL-1.2. The first located root grant-bearing commit is 2020-10-01: https://github.com/Sudwest-Fryslan/OpenZaakBrug/commit/4a40f8c152da6247c6833dc75db966d4541199f0.

primary_evidence.note: The exact project README states Súdwest-Fryslân went into production in 2021, Haarlem in 2023, and Den Haag in 2024, lists supported legacy applications, and links installation guidance. Version 1.2.21 was released on 2025-11-21: https://github.com/Sudwest-Fryslan/OpenZaakBrug/releases/tag/1.2.21.

review.product_identity: Open Zaakbrug (legacy ZDS-to-ZGW migration and replication bridge)
review.agency: Municipality of Súdwest-Fryslân (initial collaboration with Utrecht and Haarlem; VNG innovation subsidy)
review.license: EUPL-1.2
review.family_note: The Súdwest-Fryslân repository is the maintained municipal fork of Haarlem/zds-stuf-to-zgw-api-translator and the versioned Open Zaakbrug implementation used in production. Treat it and its Haarlem ancestor as one bridge product family, not two independent products; it is distinct from OpenZaak itself.
review.status_note: First located source snapshot with the EUPL grant is 2020-10-01; repository creation predates that. A versioned 1.2.21 release and installation guide are current, and the repository was active in September 2026.

review.decision_reason: La Suite Calc is a DINUM-sponsored collaborative-spreadsheet prototype/fork of Docs, but its README still describes it as a prototype and provides only local test/development setup. The repository has no versioned releases or installation/user guidance for an operational service or independently reusable product; the current official La Suite spreadsheet offering is Grist, not this Calc prototype.

government_provenance.note: The project publiccode manifest identifies DINUM as funder and user, and the license names Direction interministérielle du numérique as copyright holder. This establishes a government project relationship, not operational adoption of the prototype.

public_source.note: The repository is public and provides the prototype source and local development materials.

eligible_license.note: The top-level LICENSE and README grant MIT for this repository. The first commit adding the spreadsheet-specific IronCalc integration is https://github.com/suitenumerique/calc/commit/92c72c80f4d5e049f99631d0d816135018f47586 (2025-06-02); the repository also has an earlier MIT license commit.

primary_evidence.note: The repository describes itself as a prototype and warns that the documented local setup is for testing purposes. It publishes no versioned releases. The current official La Suite product page identifies Grist, used by 15 ministries, as its collaborative spreadsheet: https://lasuite.numerique.gouv.fr/produits/grist. No current official Calc deployment or product-specific reuse evidence was found.

primary_evidence.note: The official terms describe operational file-storage, sharing, and browser co-editing, DINUM operation, and production service access; the README identifies the DINUM production instance and documents Kubernetes deployment.

review.decision_reason: La Suite Meet is an operational, self-hostable video-conferencing application used in production by DINUM and ANCT, with full user and deployment documentation. The repository contains a direct MIT grant for repository-authored code; separately licensed dependencies and Etalab-licensed textual/visual content are not included in that blanket claim.

government_provenance.note: The first-party government product documentation names La Suite Meet, says DINUM uses it in production for Visio, lists public DINUM and ANCT instances, and links the exact GitHub source repository. The publiccode manifest separately names DINUM as organisation/funder and maintainers.

public_source.note: The repository is public and contains Django/React application source, deployment files, tests, docs, and a license directory.

eligible_license.note: The repository includes an actual MIT grant naming DINUM/Etalab. The code snapshot and grant co-exist by the 2025-03-15 license update commit at https://github.com/suitenumerique/meet/commit/4199328a4a302a33077d917b29e6fcf0c30daff9. `LICENSES` also contains Etalab-2.0 for specified content; dependencies retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: Current first-party docs identify Meet as the production engine for Visio at visio.numerique.gouv.fr and list an ANCT production instance; the same docs provide user guides, Docker Compose/Kubernetes deployment, configuration, and upgrade instructions.

review.decision_reason: WuppieFuzz is TNO’s supported coverage-guided REST API fuzzer, with an Apache-2.0 source release, installation/tutorial guidance, current versioned installers, and an exact TNO release article. TNO also cites a 2026 scientific publication specifically about this implementation. Third-party dependencies keep their separate licenses.

government_provenance.note: TNO’s official article identifies its new REST API fuzzer, describes the exact tool, links its GitHub repository, and states TNO made it open source. TNO identifies itself as an organisation governed by public law: https://www.tno.nl/en/about-tno/organisation/.

public_source.note: The public Rust source includes a CLI fuzzer, builds, tests, tutorials, release workflows, installers, and a current publiccode.yml.

eligible_license.note: The v1.0.0 release tree contains an Apache-2.0 LICENSE and Cargo.toml identifying TNO as package author. Third-party crates are not relicensed by this grant; their terms are enumerated separately in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.

primary_evidence.note: The official TNO article explains the fuzzer’s end-user function, says it is freely available under Apache-2.0, and links a tutorial. The repository offers installable releases and cites a 2026 paper about WuppieFuzz itself.

review.product_identity: WuppieFuzz (coverage-guided REST API fuzzing CLI)
review.agency: Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO)
review.license: Apache-2.0 (TNO-authored project code; bundled dependencies retain their own licenses)
review.family_note: WuppieFuzz core is distinct from TNO-S3’s separate language-specific coverage-agent and dashboard repositories; this review does not extend the license or decision to those repos.
review.status_note: First directly verified licensed functional distribution is release v1.0.0 (2024-09-12), whose tree contains both the source and Apache grant. The current publiccode.yml calls the project stable and identifies TNO; latest observed release v1.7.1 was 2026-08-26. The 2026 citation is product-specific: Rooijakkers et al., “WuppieFuzz: Coverage-Guided, Stateful REST API Fuzzing.”

eligible_license.note: Inspected the root Apache-2.0 license. It covers the repository’s site source; referenced tools, articles, and linked third-party resources remain under their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The README defines the product as a curated list/catalog of SBOM tools, frameworks, blogs, and other media, rendered as a static comparison site.
