review.decision_reason: Hold: the exact source headers affirm that the software was developed by NIST employees and is public domain within the United States, but the repository root LICENSE.md is NIST’s older general data/work grant, not the current NIST Software licensing statement. That data/work grant conditions use on NIST acknowledgment, and no current repository file explicitly applies the OSI-approved NIST-Software text. The strict worldwide license gate is therefore unresolved pending either an exact NIST Software grant in the repository or official confirmation that this older data/work notice grants equivalent worldwide software rights.

government_provenance.note: NIST identifies the exact ELFT evaluation, explains that participants must implement its API and submit for test, and links validation/API documentation; the repository README names the NIST ELFT team.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes ELFT API headers, validation code and documentation without credentials; the official NIST test page links its API and GitHub validation instructions.

eligible_license.note: Current root LICENSE.md contains NIST's general data/work notice and acknowledgment condition, not the NIST Software notice. The project code header separately says the software is public domain within the United States (https://github.com/usnistgov/elft/blob/master/elft_1_x/include/elft.h); it does not establish a worldwide public-domain dedication. Hold for an exact NIST-Software grant or official confirmation that the old notice covers this software worldwide.

primary_evidence.note: NIST's API documentation says this exact API must be implemented to participate in ELFT and describes the submitted shared-library integration; NIST's official results include 2026 participant completion records.

review.product_identity: Evaluation of Latent Friction Ridge Technology (ELFT) participant API and validation kit
review.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Information Technology Laboratory, Biometrics Group
review.geography: United States (federal NIST evaluation; participant submissions are international)
review.license: NIST general data/work grant in root LICENSE.md; source headers state U.S. public domain; worldwide software-license scope unresolved
review.status_note: Active; NIST reports current ELFT participation and 2026 results. ELFT remains a distinct latent-mark evaluation whose API is pending unification under the broader FRIF umbrella; do not merge solely by parent program. License hold: require the exact NIST Software grant or official confirmation that the older data/work notice covers software worldwide.

review.decision_reason: Hold: the exact source headers affirm that the software was developed by NIST employees and is public domain within the United States, but the repository root LICENSE.md is NIST’s older general data/work grant, not the current NIST Software licensing statement. That data/work grant conditions use on NIST acknowledgment, and no current repository file explicitly applies the OSI-approved NIST-Software text. The strict worldwide license gate is therefore unresolved pending either an exact NIST Software grant in the repository or official confirmation that this older data/work notice grants equivalent worldwide software rights.

government_provenance.note: NIST identifies FRIF as its public technology-evaluation program, states the program is ongoing, and describes the umbrella and the tests/API components; repository README names the NIST FRIF team.

public_source.note: The public repository contains FRIF common/API headers and documentation. NIST-hosted Doxygen exposes the same versioned API and links to the program's participant documentation.

eligible_license.note: Current root LICENSE.md contains NIST's general data/work notice and acknowledgment condition, not the NIST Software notice. The project code header separately says the software is public domain within the United States (https://github.com/usnistgov/frifte/blob/main/include/frifte/frifte.h); it does not establish a worldwide public-domain dedication. Hold for an exact NIST-Software grant or official confirmation that the old notice covers this software worldwide.

primary_evidence.note: The NIST-hosted API reference names the FRIF API, shows its version 1.2.0 interface and describes participant-facing template input/output types; NIST's official program page confirms current evaluation activity and user documentation.

review.product_identity: FRIF common API and participant documentation for NIST friction-ridge technology evaluations
review.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Information Technology Laboratory
review.geography: United States (federal standard/evaluation program with international participants)
review.license: NIST general data/work grant in root LICENSE.md; source headers state U.S. public domain; worldwide software-license scope unresolved
review.status_note: Active; current NIST program and API reference show version 1.2.0. Product-family review should distinguish this common/umbrella API from separate pending-unification ELFT, MINEX and SlapSeg repositories. License hold: require the exact NIST Software grant or official confirmation that the older data/work notice covers software worldwide.

review.decision_reason: The repository is a genuine public-domain NIST/IARPA API for submissions to the 2017 Nail-to-Nail Fingerprint Challenge, but the exact challenge completed in December 2019 and its API repository stopped substantive changes in 2021. The API existed only to validate participant submissions for that closed event; no current deployment, support or exact-code use was found. With more than 48 months of source quiet and no current-use evidence, it does not meet the freshness baseline for a new product record.

government_provenance.note: NIST identifies the exact IARPA-funded challenge, its collaboration with NIST/JHU APL, and NIST's role in providing the custom submission API.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the N2N participant API, validation instructions and test-plan documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The direct project LICENSE states NIST/IARPA employee work is public domain in the United States. Its worldwide rights grant carries attribution and modification-notice conditions; it was included at initial publication in 2017.

primary_evidence.note: NIST states the challenge ran January 2017–December 2019 and is completed; the API serves that challenge's validation/submission workflow, and no current exact-code use or support is evidenced.

review.product_identity: IARPA Nail-to-Nail Fingerprint Challenge participant API and validation package
review.agency: Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity (IARPA) with NIST; NIST Information Technology Laboratory performed data/image analysis
review.geography: United States (federal challenge; international research participants)
review.license: U.S. public domain; worldwide permission conditioned on NIST/IARPA attribution and modification notices
review.status_note: Rejected for new intake: the challenge ended in 2019 and the API has no evidenced current use; last repository change was October 2021. Family lineage: README says API is based on NIST FpVTE 2012 API, but it was a challenge-specific implementation.

review.decision_reason: Hold: the exact source headers affirm that the software was developed by NIST employees and is public domain within the United States, but the repository root LICENSE.md is NIST’s older general data/work grant, not the current NIST Software licensing statement. That data/work grant conditions use on NIST acknowledgment, and no current repository file explicitly applies the OSI-approved NIST-Software text. The strict worldwide license gate is therefore unresolved pending either an exact NIST Software grant in the repository or official confirmation that this older data/work notice grants equivalent worldwide software rights.

government_provenance.note: NIST identifies MINEX III as its continuing INCITS 378 template test and says the test establishes compliance for the U.S. Government PIV program; repository README describes its MINEX III code/examples.

public_source.note: The public repository contains MINEX III source/examples and participant documentation without credentials; NIST's current MINEX site provides evaluation and result documentation.

eligible_license.note: Current root LICENSE.md contains NIST's general data/work notice and acknowledgment condition, not the NIST Software notice. The project code header separately says the software is public domain within the United States (https://github.com/usnistgov/minex/blob/master/minexiii/validation/minexiii.h); it does not establish a worldwide public-domain dedication. Hold for an exact NIST-Software grant or official confirmation that the old notice covers this software worldwide.

primary_evidence.note: NIST-hosted MINEX III tables show participant submissions completed through September 2026, establishing continuing use of the exact API/test product; official NIST overview identifies the test's federal PIV compliance role.

review.product_identity: MINEX III participant code and examples for interoperable minutiae-template generation/matching evaluation
review.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Information Technology Laboratory
review.geography: United States (federal PIV standard/evaluation; international vendors participate)
review.license: NIST general data/work grant in root LICENSE.md; source headers state U.S. public domain; worldwide software-license scope unresolved
review.status_note: Active/Maintained; current MINEX III result tables were updated through September 2026 and its official page says the test is continuing. FRIF describes PIV 1:1 comparison as MINEX and pending unification; preserve exact API/product lineage for coordinator dedup review. License hold: require the exact NIST Software grant or official confirmation that the older data/work notice covers software worldwide.

review.decision_reason: Hold: the exact source headers affirm that the software was developed by NIST employees and is public domain within the United States, but the repository root LICENSE.md is NIST’s older general data/work grant, not the current NIST Software licensing statement. That data/work grant conditions use on NIST acknowledgment, and no current repository file explicitly applies the OSI-approved NIST-Software text. The strict worldwide license gate is therefore unresolved pending either an exact NIST Software grant in the repository or official confirmation that this older data/work notice grants equivalent worldwide software rights.

government_provenance.note: NIST describes SlapSeg as its ongoing evaluation, identifies SlapSeg III as the current test, and provides official participant/test information; the repository README names the NIST SlapSeg team.

public_source.note: The public repository includes the SlapSeg III API implementation, validation package and documentation; NIST-hosted API pages expose the same version 1.2.0 interface.

eligible_license.note: Current root LICENSE.md contains NIST's general data/work notice and acknowledgment condition, not the NIST Software notice. The project code header separately says the software is public domain within the United States (https://github.com/usnistgov/slapseg/blob/master/slapsegiii/include/slapsegiii.h); it does not establish a worldwide public-domain dedication. Hold for an exact NIST-Software grant or official confirmation that the old notice covers this software worldwide.

primary_evidence.note: NIST's live SlapSeg III results page records current participant submissions, including a September 15, 2026 completion at API version 1.2.0; NIST's official program page marks the evaluation ongoing.

review.product_identity: SlapSeg III participant API and validation tools for fingerprint segmentation evaluation
review.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Information Technology Laboratory
review.geography: United States (federal evaluation; international commercial participants)
review.license: NIST general data/work grant in root LICENSE.md; source headers state U.S. public domain; worldwide software-license scope unresolved
review.status_note: Active; a participant completed the current 1.2.0 API on 2026-09-15. This repository carries SlapSeg III source, first visible in 2022 and changed substantively through August 2025; the FRIF program page labels SlapSeg as pending unification, so confirm migration/source parity before deduplicating against frifte. License hold: require the exact NIST Software grant or official confirmation that the older data/work notice covers software worldwide.

review.decision_reason: Hold pending rights/scope confirmation for the original trec_eval code. NIST's 2024 LICENSE.md gives broad reuse rights for NIST-developed modifications, but states that code through version 9 is copyright Chris Buckley; the core trec_eval.c still carries a research-only, non-commercial permission notice. The repository is public and directly associated with NIST TREC, but the current top-level notice does not clearly resolve commercial use of the original code, so no eligible-license result or first licensed-source year can be assigned.

government_provenance.note: NIST's official TREC site identifies trec_eval as its evaluation software; the current repository is in the usnistgov organization and its README identifies the Text Retrieval Conference evaluation use.

public_source.note: The canonical NIST repository is public and exposes the evaluation code, documentation, and release history.

eligible_license.note: The NIST grant permits reuse of NIST-developed software and modifications, but the same notice attributes original code through version 9 to Chris Buckley. The core source file separately restricts use and modification to research, non-commercial purposes (https://github.com/usnistgov/trec_eval/blob/main/trec_eval.c); this apparent scope conflict needs rights-holder clarification. LICENSE.md itself was added 2024-01-15 (https://github.com/usnistgov/trec_eval/commit/f222e22fb8c50c81b106e5d143d80a381ff7028e), but no defensible year of fully eligible licensed source is established.

primary_evidence.note: NIST's official TREC page documents trec_eval as the evaluation program for the conference and links project information; the repository README describes the software's identity and use.

review.product_identity: TREC trec_eval information-retrieval evaluation software
review.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Information Technology Laboratory; original code by Chris Buckley
review.license: NIST reuse grant for NIST-developed modifications; original code carries a research/non-commercial restriction pending scope clarification

review.decision_reason: Visualize is the currently operated federal web application for creating and embedding visualizations from Swiss open government data. The exact public repository identifies FOEN and other federal authorities as developers, contains its BSD-3-Clause source grant, and provides public user/developer/deployment documentation.

government_provenance.note: The exact README says FOEN and other federal authorities develop the application and that it is operated at visualize.admin.ch; this is project-specific attribution, not inference from the organization name.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the web application, docs, changelog, deployment setup, and source files without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE contains a direct standard BSD-3-Clause grant naming FOEN; the first located license-bearing source commit is 02d8d648b4bff7c20f3ba7f3f9e5be30dfeeb315.

primary_evidence.note: The live federal portal allows users to browse Swiss OGD datasets and start visualization; its current interface reports v6.5.0. Repository docs cover creating/embedding charts and local/deployed setup.

review.product_identity: Visualize, the visualize.admin.ch web application for creating and embedding visualizations from Swiss Open Government Data
review.agency: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN), with other Swiss federal authorities
review.license: BSD-3-Clause
review.family_note: This is the visualization application, distinct from the LINDAS linked-data service that supplies/query-hosts datasets and the federal OGD catalog.
review.status_note: The canonical GitHub repository existed from 2019, but the first located post-creation source snapshot with the BSD-3-Clause grant is commit 02d8d648b4bff7c20f3ba7f3f9e5be30dfeeb315 (2020-05-01); use 2020 as first evidenced public licensed source. The live application remains available with current public documentation.

Its public source and product documentation do not cure that license-gate failure.

government_provenance.note: The official product website describes Prodige and links this exact repository, and describes shared user governance; the reviewed material did not establish a named public-body rights-holder/commissioning agency for this repository. Do not treat the SILL/inventory entry or group name as agency proof.

public_source.note: The linked public GitLab project exposes its 4.4 branch; its README and LICENSE.md are directly retrievable from the repository raw routes despite the GitLab web UI’s bot-check limitation.

eligible_license.note: The file explicitly grants CeCILL-B. The methodology requires an exact OSI-approved grant; CeCILL-B does not appear in the OSI-approved license list (https://opensource.org/licenses/). Do not substitute the separate CeCILL-2.1 license or another Prodige repository.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party product site describes the operational territorial data-infrastructure platform and links the exact assigned repository; its public training manual documents application use/configuration. This is not evidence of an eligible grant.

government_provenance.note: The exact product’s user manual identifies Madis as an open-source application designed by Soluris. The assigned repository is in Soluris’s own ADULLACT group. Soluris is a public inter-municipal digital-services syndicate; this is not merely an inventory attribution.

public_source.note: The exact public GitLab project contains the PHP/Symfony web application, frontend assets, migrations, tests, deployment files, installation documentation, and changelog.

eligible_license.note: The repository root LICENSE.md is the full GNU Affero General Public License version 3 text; the project README links to it as Madis’s license. AGPL-3.0 is OSI-approved. This claim is for the assigned Madis source, not sibling Madis Cyber or external dependencies.

primary_evidence.note: Soluris’s exact Madis product page describes the GDPR-compliance software for territorial public bodies; the current user manual documents actual application workflows. Soluris’s 2024 activity report also describes Madis installations and training for public digital-services operators. Current source tags include v2.6.0 (17 Sep 2026).

review.decision_reason: This is a public codebase for the live Dutch government developer portal, but the assigned Digilab repository’s publiccode.yml points to the older Common Ground/DON repository as canonical source, while its current publiccode names Geonovum as source owner and its README retains a VNG Realisatie 2019 copyright/license notice. It also appears to overlap the separately reviewed API Register, OSS Register, register-site, and knowledge-site repositories. Hold until the current production source boundary, ownership history, and umbrella-versus-component catalog identity are resolved.

government_provenance.note: Geonovum’s 2024 execution plan explicitly says the developer.overheid.nl provision is developed under the Ministry of BZK’s Data bij de Bron program. The exact assigned repo README says it contains the software backing that portal; current publiccode.yml names Stichting Geonovum as code/repository owner, while historical README/license material credits VNG Realisatie.

public_source.note: The assigned GitLab project is publicly readable and contains web, API, data, deployment, and container source. Its README identifies it as software backing developer.overheid.nl.

eligible_license.note: The current source has an EUPL-1.2 root license and publiccode.yml claim. Its publiccode points to the older Common Ground/DON source, whose actual LICENCE.md grants EUPL-1.2 with VNG Realisatie copyright: https://gitlab.com/commonground/don/developer.overheid.nl/-/commit/f7e954952bc9b78495a0b7e70ffc44ed3b3a1ef9. Resolve code-owner history and whether the current copy’s complete additions are in grant scope before admission.

primary_evidence.note: The live official site describes the Dutch government developer portal, and the assigned README says this repo backs it. The full monorepo appears to overlap separately reviewed portal repositories (`don-api-register`, `don-oss-register`, `don-register-site`, and `don-site`); no authoritative current deployment map established whether this repo is the production umbrella, a legacy implementation, or a parallel codebase.

review.product_identity: Developer Overheid portal software (full-stack API and OSS discovery portal; umbrella/legacy boundary unresolved)
review.agency: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations (BZK) program; Geonovum is named by current publiccode as source/repository owner; VNG Realisatie is credited by the historical EUPL notice
review.license: EUPL-1.2 (portal source; repository ownership/attribution and current additions need reconciliation)
review.family_note: Potential umbrella for the separately reviewed Developer Overheid API Register, OSS Register, shared register-site frontend, and knowledge portal. Avoid a duplicate umbrella/component product entry until the current production deployment boundary is confirmed.
review.status_note: Current Digilab project was created in 2024; its publiccode.yml points to the Common Ground/DON canonical source. The older upstream has a directly inspected EUPL-1.2 grant-bearing commit in 2019. Do not treat that as proof that every later Digilab contribution or every separately linked component is covered.

review.decision_reason: This is a public, working reference implementation with source, a live demo, and EUPL terms. Hold because its README still describes LDV as a draft and its conformance claim has not been mapped to Logius's finalized 1.0.0 standard; no versioned release or official production/adoption record for this exact implementation resolves that gap. Clear with current conformance documentation or an official deployment/adoption record tied to this code.

government_provenance.note: The exact government-hosted project metadata identifies Geonovum as main copyright owner and scopes the software to the Dutch government; the repository is published in the Digilab.overheid.nl Logboek Dataverwerkingen group. Logius identifies the Ministry of BZK as responsible for the standard and Logius as its manager: https://www.logius.nl/onze-dienstverlening/gegevensuitwisseling/logboek-dataverwerkingen/over-logboek-dataverwerkingen.

public_source.note: The public repository includes a multi-service implementation, developer setup instructions, tests, and a live demo link; the initial source tree already contains functional backend and frontend code.

eligible_license.note: The exact repository contains the full EUPL-1.2 text and publiccode.yml declares EUPL-1.2 with Geonovum as the main copyright owner. This decision covers the repository-authored program, not separately licensed dependencies.

primary_evidence.note: This live, project-specific demo describes the reference implementation and demonstrates user-facing LDV logging. However, the repo README calls the standard a draft while Logius now publishes finalized LDV 1.0.0 (https://gitdocumentatie.logius.nl/publicatie/logboek/dataverwerkingen/1.0.0/); no exact-version conformance mapping, versioned release, or official operational-use record establishes that this demo implements the finalized standard.

review.product_identity: LDV Reference Implementation (distributed data-processing log and transparency demo)
review.agency: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations (standard sponsor); Geonovum (repository copyright owner); Logius (standard manager)
review.license: EUPL-1.2 for repository-authored code; dependencies retain their own terms
review.family_note: This is a reference implementation/demo of the Logius LDV standard, not the normative standard itself. Do not merge its software license with the separately published standard documentation.
review.status_note: The first inspected public commit (2025-05-16) contains functional source and the EUPL-1.2 license text. The project is explicitly marked development and has no GitLab releases/tags. Reassess when the project documents conformance to LDV 1.0.0 or an official agency records use of this exact build.

review.decision_reason: LX-core is public and the current README explicitly grants EUPL-1.2-or-later to the program except files with different notices. Hold because this repository calls itself a 2025 revised LinkeXtractor version published for review, has no versioned release, and the official service page documents LinkeXtractor generally without showing that the deployed product uses this new core. government_provenance.note: KOOP's official page names and describes the exact LinkeXtractor product; its README states LX-core is the new version replacing the older implementation.
